items.title: Maria Bartiromo Out at Fox News, Fox Business
items.summary:
Fox News Media has parted ways with Maria Bartiromo, ending a run of more than 12 years across Fox News Channel and Fox Business Network. The company confirmed the exit in a statement on Thursday, the same day her final edition of "Mornings with Maria" aired on Fox Business.

"We thank Maria for her work over the last 12 1/2 years and wish her all the best on her next chapter," the company said, per Variety, which reported the departure. Fox offered no explanation for the timing.

The network is redistributing her programs rather than replacing her. "Mornings with Maria" becomes "Morning with Fox Business" and will use a rotation of anchors. "Maria Bartiromo's Wall Street," the Friday weekly on FBN, is being renamed "FBN's Wall Street," with Cheryl Casone hosting this week and rotating anchors after that.

On Fox News Channel, Jason Chaffetz will take over "Sunday Morning Futures" this week, the long-running Sunday show Bartiromo anchored. Fox said a permanent host will be named later.

Fox Business also plans to roll out a new daytime programming schedule in the coming weeks. Bartiromo built her reputation at CNBC covering Wall Street before moving to the Fox networks, where she anchored a morning show, a weekly markets program and a Sunday politics hour. Her next move has not been announced.

items.title: Camilo Séptimo Keyboardist Jonathan Meléndez, His Pregnant Wife and 3-Year Old Daughter Murdered in Mexico
items.summary:
Jonathan Meléndez, keyboardist and a founding member of the Mexican band Camilo Séptimo, was found murdered at his home outside Mexico City along with his wife, their 3-year-old daughter and the family's nanny. The State of Mexico Prosecutor's Office confirmed the killings, which took place in a residential complex in the municipality of Atizapán de Zaragoza.

Authorities said Ana Paula Meléndez, 35, was four months pregnant. A 6-year-old child was found alive and unharmed inside the home. The nanny was 21. Three of the four victims were shot in the head and one was shot in the back, according to the prosecutor's statement; the family dog was found tied up.

Two men have been arrested, Mexico's secretary of public security Omar García Harfuch said in a statement reported by Variety and CNN. He said one suspect, identified in part as Diego Sebastián N, was a business partner of one of the victims and allegedly used that relationship to gain entry to the residence.

Camilo Séptimo posted a tribute to Meléndez on social media. "Today we honor and celebrate his life, his music, his light, and what he shared with those of us fortunate enough to know him and walk alongside him," the band wrote.

Meléndez formed the group in Mexico City in 2013 with singer Manuel Mendoza and guitarist Erik Vázquez. After an EP in 2014, the band released its debut album "Óleos" in 2017, which reached No. 10 on the Mexican albums chart, and followed it with three more records, most recently "Jardín de las almas" in 2023. The investigation into the killings is continuing.

items.title: Noel Gallagher Hints at Oasis 2027 Summer Tour
items.summary:
Noel Gallagher has come as close as he ever does to confirming that Oasis will tour again in 2027. Asked directly about the rumors during an appearance on talkSPORT's "Drive," the guitarist deflected before landing on a reason the band might be free next summer.

Gallagher first pointed the finger at his brother, joking, "It's Liam, isn't it? He's not into it. He's not into Oasis anymore." When host Andy Goldstein noted that Liam had recently quit social media, Gallagher shifted. "Well, then there must be something happening," he said, according to Rolling Stone. "Well, let's put it this way: there's no football tournament on next year, so we've got to do something in the summer, right?"

The band has confirmed nothing. Reports have circulated about another large-scale run, possibly including a return to Knebworth, where Oasis played to 250,000 people across two nights in 1996. Liam Gallagher shot down one specific rumor last month, telling fans on social media that a 2027 Glastonbury headline slot was "not happening so all you croc wearing flag waving shit cunts can calm the fuck down."

The hints are not new. Oasis spent most of 2025 on their reunion tour, and when the band wrapped its London dates in September, Noel thanked the crowd and said, "Most of all, I wanna thank you lot for keeping the faith and putting this band back on the map," adding moments later: "See you next year!"

In the meantime, the band has a film on the way. "Don't Look Back in Anger," written by "Peaky Blinders" creator Steven Knight and directed by Dylan Southern and Will Lovelace, opens in IMAX theaters on Sept. 11 before moving to Hulu and Disney+ later this year. Knight said the documentary includes Liam and Noel sitting down together "for the first time in 15 years."

items.title: Neil Peart Documentary No One’s Disciple Gets First Trailer
items.summary:
The Canadian Broadcasting Corporation has released the first trailer for "No One's Disciple," a documentary about Neil Peart, the Rush drummer and lyricist who died in 2020. Scot McFadyen and Sam Dunn co-directed the film, which premieres at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 16.

Peart's surviving bandmates Geddy Lee and Alex Lifeson both appear as interview subjects, as do drummers Chad Smith of the Red Hot Chili Peppers and Stewart Copeland of the Police. "After Neil passed away, we never really were able to pay tribute to him," Lee says in the trailer. "And that weighed on me a lot."

The preview also draws on archival interviews with Peart himself. In one clip he recalls his introduction to the instrument: "When I started to get around 11 or 12 years old I was banging around the house and smashing up pots and pans, and my parents got the idea that I liked to hit things with sticks."

As Pitchfork noted, a wide release date has not been set. Lee and Lifeson are in the middle of their Fifty Something World Tour, with Anika Nilles handling drums.

items.title: Watch Ariana Grande Make Her Play for Robert De Niro’s Circle of Trust in ‘Focker-in-Law’ Trailer
items.summary:
Paramount Pictures released a new international trailer for "Focker-in-Law" on Thursday (Sept. 3), giving a fuller look at Ariana Grande's role in the fourth installment of the Meet the Parents franchise. The film opens in theaters Nov. 25, over Thanksgiving weekend.

Grande plays Olivia Jones, a California life coach dating Henry Focker (Skyler Gisondo), the son of Greg Focker (Ben Stiller). Henry wants to propose; Greg isn't sold. The trailer sets up a family weekend in which Greg borrows his own father-in-law's playbook to vet Olivia, with Robert De Niro back as Jack Byrnes and the series' lie detector rig making a return appearance. Olivia handles it, putting out a kitchen fire Greg starts and performing the Heimlich on him when he chokes.

The trailer is set to RAYE's "Where Is My Husband!," which peaked at No. 11 on the Billboard Hot 100. The cast also includes newcomer Eduardo Franco alongside returning players Owen Wilson as Kevin, Teri Polo as Pam Focker, Beanie Feldstein as Samantha Focker and Blythe Danner as Dina Byrnes.

Grande had said she would be "taking a step back from visibility" after finishing her Eternal Sunshine Tour, but Billboard confirmed Wednesday that she will participate in press and promotion for the film because she is proud of it. She closed the tour Tuesday (Sept. 1) with a tenth London show; according to Billboard Boxscore, the run grossed $107.9 million from 638,000 tickets sold.
